headline: IRC Adds Modern Features Without Leaving IRC
lede: IRCv3 extends the old protocol with SASL, metadata, timestamps, history, and account tooling. The mandate is compatibility: add contemporary capabilities without breaking the networks and clients that endured.

headline: LineageOS 24 Extends Android 17’s Reach
lede: LineageOS 24.0 brings Android 17, redesigned core apps, a new updater, and broader device support. Commonized kernels, WebUSB flashing, and documented virtual targets make the release easier to maintain—and easier to install.

headline: Nitter Asks for Help Under Legal Pressure
lede: X Corp. has sent cease-and-desist letters to Nitter instances and its repository. The open-source alternative is now seeking funding and legal counsel to preserve a privacy-oriented window onto X.

headline: A Small Language Model Becomes a Decision Engine
lede: A single next-token distribution can turn a language model into a fast fixed-choice classifier. The method is practical, but its raw confidence is not trustworthy until calibration gives the numbers meaning.
pullquote: A prediction is only useful when its confidence has earned the right to be believed.

headline: A Weekend Physics Experiment Drives GTA
lede: A 1996 Atari ST prototype models forces, torque, collisions, and tires with surprising coherence. Rebuilt in the browser, its cars, ships, and bricks show how low-level mechanics can become a game’s signature feel.

headline: This City Builder Wants Fewer Buildings
lede: Discretionary Review turns San Francisco housing approvals into a playable maze of sites, appeals, lawsuits, financing, and delay. Every proposed home enters a game where regulations change, cash burns, and the city can simply say no.

headline: The Ceiling Becomes the Computer Screen
lede: The Lightbulb Computer projects shared interfaces onto walls, counters, and everyday objects. Its working prototype pairs vision, voice, and gestures with a harder engineering question: how can an always-aware room remain private?

headline: What a Git Commit Actually Weighs
lede: A commit’s disk cost depends on object overhead, compressibility, repository structure, and later packing. Tiny changes can occupy kilobytes in loose storage, while larger and repetitive files benefit substantially from deduplication and delta compression.

headline: Language Models Return to the Byte Stream
lede: Byte-level models discard the fixed vocabulary and operate closer to the raw signal of text. That may help with multilingual input, code, symbols, and adversarial noise, while demanding new compromises in efficiency and design.

headline: A PSP Gets a Raspberry Pi Second Life
lede: PSPi 6 replaces the original motherboard with a Raspberry Pi while preserving the handheld’s controls, shell, and screen. The result is a documented Linux-capable retrofit for aging hardware—part preservation project, part electronics challenge.
